title: Analytic maps keep right angles
lede: A square grid in the complex plane is carried to w = (1 − t)z + t f(z). Teal lines were horizontal, red lines were vertical; the faint grid is where they started.
notice: Wherever the derivative is not zero, a teal line and a red line still cross at 90 degrees, however much the squares are bent and stretched. This is what conformal means.
Each little square stays nearly a square: it is rotated and scaled, not sheared. Drag the dot and read the angle.
At a critical point (gold ring) the derivative is zero and the angle doubles, so z² turns the corner at 0 into a straight line. At a pole such as 0 for 1/z, the grid is clipped.
hint: Drag on the stage to move the dot. Slide t to morph from the identity.
